title: Closed-loop validation of training-only language supervision for autonomous driving
current_belief: Training-only task-decomposed language supervision can improve open-loop driving metrics without retaining an autoregressive language model at inference.
proposed_challenge: Open-loop collision improvements may not survive when the learned planner changes the state distribution it subsequently observes.
scientific_question: Does training-only task-decomposed language supervision reduce closed-loop intervention and collision rates relative to the same driving policy trained without language supervision?
falsifiable_claim: Across at least three closed-loop driving scenarios and five seeds, task-decomposed language supervision will reduce intervention rate by at least 10% relative without increasing route-completion error by more than 2 percentage points; failure to meet both thresholds falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied TaLS record reports metric-specific open-loop gains and the supplied CoRL call establishes current robot-learning interest, but neither constitutes closed-loop evidence or novelty proof.
reasoning_summary: TaLS motivates a language-supervised driving intervention, while the closed-loop estimator study shows that excellent offline accuracy can fail after feedback changes the input distribution. The candidate directly tests whether that failure mode transfers to end-to-end driving.
cheap_falsifier: Run matched policies in one simulator town with three weather shifts and three seeds; kill the idea if language supervision does not improve intervention rate in at least two shifts.
main_risk: Simulator interventions may not predict physical-vehicle safety outcomes.

title: Stage-local causal attribution for task-decomposed language supervision
current_belief: Perception, motion, risk, and planning language states can each be injected during training, but aggregate performance does not identify which stage carries the safety gain.
proposed_challenge: The reported benefit may be concentrated in one stage or may arise from generic extra supervision rather than the semantic decomposition.
scientific_question: Which stage-specific language representation is necessary for the collision reduction attributed to task-decomposed supervision?
falsifiable_claim: Under matched training compute, removing the risk-stage representation will recover at least 50% of the total collision-rate degradation produced by removing all language representations, whereas removing any single non-risk stage will recover less than 30%; any incompatible ordering falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied driving study exposes a four-stage training chain and reports partial pathway evidence, while the ICRA call supplies venue-interest evidence only.
reasoning_summary: The source reports a structured supervision path but does not identify the necessary stage. A matched stage-deletion matrix turns the architectural story into a causal, falsifiable mechanism test.
cheap_falsifier: Retrain a small model on 20% of the data with all-language, no-language, and four single-stage deletions; stop if the estimated stage effects are indistinguishable within bootstrap intervals.
main_risk: Interactions among stages may make single-deletion effects non-additive and difficult to interpret.

title: Attention-support drift as a transfer-risk marker for adapted robot vision-language policies
current_belief: Low-rank adaptation often preserves out-of-domain vision-language transfer better than full fine-tuning, and broader retained attention support correlates descriptively with transfer retention.
proposed_challenge: Classification attention drift may not predict embodied policy failure once language grounding and action decoding are coupled.
scientific_question: Does pre-to-post adaptation attention-support drift predict held-out embodiment success more accurately than in-domain validation accuracy?
falsifiable_claim: Across two adaptation methods, three learning rates, and at least four held-out task families, attention-support drift will improve failure-ranking AUROC by at least 0.05 over in-domain validation accuracy; a smaller or reversed gain falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied controlled VLM study identifies learning-rate-dependent heatmap drift, and the supplied MLLM survey frames adaptation locus and retained generality as coupled design concerns; the CoRL call indicates community interest, not novelty.
reasoning_summary: This transfers a descriptive VLM drift measurement into an embodied predictive test while explicitly comparing it against the easier in-domain metric.
cheap_falsifier: Adapt one open vision-language policy on one task at three learning rates and evaluate two unseen tasks; kill if drift and transfer failure have absolute Spearman correlation below 0.3.
main_risk: Attention statistics may be architecture-specific and non-causal.

title: Shift-adaptive LoRA rank for on-device robot test-time adaptation
current_belief: Low-rank test-time adaptation can approach full-update performance with far fewer trainable parameters, and an existing analysis links optimal rank to domain-shift magnitude.
proposed_challenge: Image-domain rank scaling may fail for sequential robot observations where errors are temporally correlated and adaptation changes the policy trajectory.
scientific_question: Does a domain-shift-conditioned LoRA rank improve the accuracy-efficiency frontier of robot perception test-time adaptation over a fixed rank?
falsifiable_claim: Across at least four visual shifts, adaptive rank selection will match fixed-rank task success within 2 percentage points while reducing median trainable parameters or adaptation FLOPs by at least 25%; failure on either criterion falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied LoRA-TTA record provides a rank-scaling hypothesis, and the supplied IROS call supplies a current robotics venue signal without establishing novelty.
reasoning_summary: The candidate tests whether the reported rank-versus-shift relationship remains useful under embodied sequential deployment and makes efficiency part of the falsification criterion.
cheap_falsifier: Use one frozen robot encoder under clean, blur, lighting, and camera-pose shifts; compare ranks 1, 2, 4, 8 against a shift-estimated choice on a small validation stream.
main_risk: Estimating shift magnitude may cost more than the parameter savings.

title: Do learned rank gates preserve closed-loop transfer in embodied vision-language adaptation?
current_belief: Rank-gated LoRA can support post-training rank removal, but the supplied prototype did not demonstrate learned sparsity or meaningful deployment savings at low initial rank.
proposed_challenge: Sparse gates may prune components that look redundant on VQA validation yet encode rare action-grounding behaviors needed in closed loop.
scientific_question: Can sparsity-regularized rank gates reduce an embodied VLM adapter without degrading held-out closed-loop task success?
falsifiable_claim: Starting from rank 32, gated pruning will remove at least 50% of rank components while retaining task success within 3 percentage points of matched fixed-rank LoRA on both trained and held-out embodiments; violation on either split falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied rank-gating study names the decisive missing experiments, while the supplied attention-drift study warns that adaptation can preserve in-domain performance yet damage transfer; the ICLR call is an interest signal only.
reasoning_summary: The candidate combines an explicit negative result about absent learned sparsity with a transfer-risk observation, producing a bounded closed-loop pruning test rather than assuming document-VQA results generalize.
cheap_falsifier: Train rank-16 gated and fixed adapters on one manipulation task, prune by half, and test one unseen camera pose; kill if pruned success falls by more than 5 points.
main_risk: Closed-loop evaluation variance may obscure small pruning effects.

title: Frequency-stratified evaluation for long-tailed robot object recognition
current_belief: Aggregate detection metrics can conceal near-failure on rare classes even when localization appears adequate.
proposed_challenge: Robot manipulation benchmarks may similarly overstate competence by averaging common household objects with safety-critical rare objects.
scientific_question: How much does frequency-stratified evaluation change the estimated competence of robot object detectors used for manipulation?
falsifiable_claim: On at least two manipulation datasets, few-shot-class AP50 will be at least 20 percentage points below aggregate AP50 for a majority of tested detectors; if the gap is smaller on both datasets, the claim is falsified.
why_now: The supplied oracle-character study demonstrates a large aggregate-versus-few-shot gap, and the NeurIPS evaluation-and-datasets call provides direct benchmark-track interest without proving the same issue in robotics.
reasoning_summary: A documented long-tail measurement failure in another visual domain motivates a direct audit of robot perception benchmarks, with a numerical gap that can be disproved cheaply.
cheap_falsifier: Re-score public predictions from one manipulation detector after binning classes by training frequency; stop if rare-class AP50 is within 10 points of aggregate AP50.
main_risk: Dataset frequency may be a poor proxy for operational importance or visual difficulty.

title: Decoupled rare-class recognition for manipulation perception
current_belief: Frequency-aware optimization inside a joint detection head may harm performance, whereas separating localization from recognition improved rare-class results in the supplied long-tail study.
proposed_challenge: The same decoupling may not help robot images because occlusion and viewpoint changes couple localization and identity.
scientific_question: Does decoupling localization and frequency-aware recognition improve rare-object manipulation success over joint detector reweighting?
falsifiable_claim: A decoupled detector will improve few-shot-class AP50 by at least 5 points and rare-object grasp success by at least 5 points over joint reweighting without reducing common-class AP50 by more than 2 points; failure of any condition falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied long-tail record reports a counterproductive naive reweighting result and a successful decoupled alternative; the CVPR call signals interest in visual methods but not transfer validity.
reasoning_summary: This is a cross-domain mechanism transfer with both perception and downstream grasp outcomes, so an AP gain alone cannot sustain the claim.
cheap_falsifier: Fine-tune a common detector on one tabletop dataset using joint reweighting versus a frozen localizer plus resampled classifier; kill if rare AP does not improve.
main_risk: Rare-class sample counts may be too small for stable downstream grasp estimates.

title: Closed-loop stress tests for offline-accurate robot state estimators
current_belief: High offline reconstruction accuracy is often treated as sufficient evidence that a learned estimator can serve as a feedback sensor.
proposed_challenge: Estimator errors can alter control actions, drive the system off the training attractor, and return as out-of-distribution observations.
scientific_question: How often does offline estimator ranking reverse when the same estimators are embedded in robot feedback control?
falsifiable_claim: Across 3 control tasks, at least 1 pair of estimators will reverse order between offline error and closed-loop success, and offline error will explain less than 50% of the variance in closed-loop success; absence of both patterns falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied closed-loop control study documents near-perfect offline correlation followed by feedback failure, and the IROS call supplies relevant venue-interest evidence only.
reasoning_summary: The candidate converts a specific control failure into a robot-estimator benchmark question focused on ranking reversals rather than another offline accuracy comparison.
cheap_falsifier: Embed two pretrained estimators in one simulated reaching controller under three perturbation levels; stop if offline and closed-loop rankings remain identical with high rank correlation.
main_risk: A poorly tuned controller could create artificial ranking reversals unrelated to estimator quality.

title: Action-consistent retraining for stabilizing learned feedback sensors
current_belief: Filtering noisy estimator outputs may delay failure, while enforcing deployment-consistent actuation and retraining on closed-loop data can address feedback-induced shift.
proposed_challenge: It is unclear whether the benefit comes from output constraints, on-policy data, or their interaction in embodied control.
scientific_question: Which intervention is necessary to stabilize a learned state estimator under robot feedback: action constraints, closed-loop retraining, or their combination?
falsifiable_claim: The combination will reduce catastrophic control failures by at least 30% over either intervention alone across three perturbation levels; a non-positive interaction or a smaller reduction falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied control record distinguishes failed smoothing remedies from a successful consistency-plus-retraining route, while the RSS call shows community interest without settling the mechanism.
reasoning_summary: A factorial intervention isolates the root cause more sharply than copying the full stabilization recipe and gives a clear negative outcome if no interaction exists.
cheap_falsifier: Run a 2x2 action-constraint by on-policy-retraining pilot in one simulated control task; kill if the combined cell does not outperform the best single intervention.
main_risk: The definition of action consistency may need task-specific engineering.

title: Ranking-disagreement uncertainty for robot instruction grounding
current_belief: Image-text retrieval confidence is usually derived from embedding uncertainty, although disagreement between global and local rankings more directly reflects returned-list risk.
proposed_challenge: Retrieval correctness may not translate into action-selection reliability when the selected object is embedded in a closed-loop instruction-following policy.
scientific_question: Does global-local ranking disagreement identify incorrect robot referent selections better than embedding entropy?
falsifiable_claim: On two referring-manipulation benchmarks, ranking disagreement will improve incorrect-selection AUROC by at least 0.05 and reduce selective-risk AURC by at least 10% relative to embedding entropy; failure on either benchmark falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied CRU study reports single-pass ranking-space uncertainty gains, and the CoRL call signals robot-learning interest but does not establish embodied transfer.
reasoning_summary: The candidate transfers a deterministic ranking-risk decomposition to instruction grounding and tests it against the standard entropy alternative on action-relevant errors.
cheap_falsifier: Compute global-local ranking disagreement from one pretrained grounding model on 500 labeled queries; kill if AUROC does not exceed entropy by 0.02.
main_risk: Some policies do not expose separable global and local ranking branches.

title: Composite applicability-aware risk for embodied policy failure
current_belief: No single uncertainty signal captures instance-level reliability across distribution shift, and model disagreement, uncertainty, and applicability-domain distance can be complementary.
proposed_challenge: A composite score may appear better only because its weights overfit one task or embodiment.
scientific_question: Does combining ensemble uncertainty, observation applicability distance, and policy disagreement improve held-out robot failure ranking over each component alone?
falsifiable_claim: Weights fit on one task family will improve failure-ranking AUROC by at least 0.05 over the best single component on two held-out task families; failure on either held-out family falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied QUAD record shows target-dependent value from composite risk, while the supplied ranking-disagreement work offers an efficient disagreement signal; the NeurIPS main call establishes broad interest only.
reasoning_summary: The design preserves the source's warning that reliability behavior is domain-dependent by requiring cross-task weight transfer rather than evaluating fitted and tested scores on the same distribution.
cheap_falsifier: Fit a linear composite on one tabletop task and test on one unseen task; stop if it fails to beat the strongest component by 0.02 AUROC.
main_risk: Applicability distance in high-dimensional multimodal observations may be poorly defined.

title: Scale-aware abstention for small embodied language models
current_belief: Cheap logit-based confidence signals degrade at small model scales, while selective multi-sample consistency can recover failure detection at additional cost.
proposed_challenge: Question-answering calibration may not predict unsafe robot decisions because sequential action errors compound and repeated samples can be correlated.
scientific_question: Can scale-aware escalation from token confidence to semantic sampling improve unsafe-action detection for small embodied language models under a fixed compute budget?
falsifiable_claim: For models at or below 3B parameters, scale-aware escalation will improve unsafe-action AUROC by at least 0.08 over temperature-scaled token confidence while using less than half the FLOPs of always sampling; failure of either condition falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied ScaleCal study documents scale-dependent confidence degradation, and the supplied MLLM survey emphasizes deployment constraints; the ICRA call contributes interest evidence only.
reasoning_summary: This candidate places the cross-scale calibration observation at a concrete embodied trust boundary and jointly tests discrimination and compute rather than assuming either transfers.
cheap_falsifier: Evaluate one 1B-scale planner on 300 safe/unsafe action choices with token confidence and four-sample consistency; kill if AUROC gain is below 0.03.
main_risk: Semantic equivalence among sampled robot actions may require task-specific judging.

title: Token-level uncertainty for timing human intervention in robot plans
current_belief: Reliability-aware training and token-level confidence can support abstention in subjective text classification.
proposed_challenge: In robot planning, uncertainty must identify the earliest action-relevant token before an irreversible step rather than merely classify the final output.
scientific_question: Does action-token uncertainty enable earlier safe intervention than sequence-level confidence in language-conditioned robot plans?
falsifiable_claim: At matched false-intervention rate, action-token uncertainty will detect at least 15% more impending failures before the last reversible action than sequence-level confidence across two planning domains; a smaller gain falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied reliability-aware DPO study motivates token-level confidence and selective prediction, while the supplied recoverability theory makes diagnostic timing and action availability explicit; the CoRL call is interest evidence only.
reasoning_summary: The candidate changes the target from final-label abstention to intervention before recoverability closes, creating an embodied temporal test rather than a direct application of text confidence.
cheap_falsifier: Replay 200 failed and successful plans, compare first threshold crossing for token- and sequence-level scores, and kill if median lead-time does not improve.
main_risk: Token boundaries may not align with executable action boundaries.

title: Action-sufficient state compression for robot control
current_belief: A predictive state preserves every history distinction affecting future distributions, although a controller may need only distinctions that change the set of acceptable actions.
proposed_challenge: A smaller action-sufficient code may fail to update recursively and therefore lose its advantage in sequential control.
scientific_question: Can an action-sufficient latent code be smaller than a predictive latent state while preserving acceptable-action coverage in sequential robot control?
falsifiable_claim: On two finite-state control tasks, an action-sufficient code will use at least 25% fewer discrete states than a predictive-state baseline while keeping unacceptable-action probability within 2 percentage points over 100-step rollouts; failure on either task falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied theoretical record separates static action sufficiency from recursive updateability, and the AISTATS call provides methodological interest evidence without an empirical result.
reasoning_summary: The study targets the exact limitation acknowledged by the source: whether static compression remains valid as an internal sequential state.
cheap_falsifier: Enumerate a small gridworld, compute predictive and action-sufficient partitions, and roll out their induced policies; kill if no compression occurs or update inconsistency raises risk.
main_risk: Finite-state demonstrations may not scale to continuous robotic systems.

title: Diagnostic information actions before robot recovery windows close
current_belief: Under partial observation, successful recovery depends on diagnostic distinguishability, elapsed diagnostic time, safety, and the remaining set of available actions.
proposed_challenge: Active-perception systems typically value information gain without explicitly pricing the loss of recoverable actions during diagnosis.
scientific_question: Does recoverability-aware diagnostic planning reduce unacceptable actions relative to information-gain-only active perception?
falsifiable_claim: In hidden-state tasks with time-limited rescue actions, recoverability-aware diagnostics will reduce unacceptable-action probability by at least 20% at matched sensing cost over information-gain-only planning; a smaller reduction falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied action-sufficiency record formalizes a diagnostic error bound and explicitly distinguishes it from outcome risk, while the RSS call signals robotics interest rather than empirical support.
reasoning_summary: The candidate operationalizes the source's recoverability distinction in a controlled robot setting and tests a policy consequence rather than treating the bound as a performance guarantee.
cheap_falsifier: Use a two-hidden-state simulator with one expiring rescue action; kill if recoverability-aware sensing does not improve risk across a grid of observation overlaps.
main_risk: Hand-designed rescue windows may make the advantage tautological.

title: Calibrated active perception thresholds for neuro-symbolic manipulation
current_belief: Uncertainty-aware symbolic planners can trigger information-gathering actions when perceptual predicate confidence falls below a threshold.
proposed_challenge: A learned threshold may exploit simulator calibration and fail under camera or object shifts, causing either wasteful sensing or unsafe action.
scientific_question: Does calibration-aware threshold selection improve active-perception utility under visual domain shift in tabletop manipulation?
falsifiable_claim: Across three visual shifts, recalibrated thresholds will reduce combined task-failure and sensing cost by at least 10% over the source-domain threshold without increasing catastrophic failures; failure on any shift falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied neuro-symbolic manipulation record reports calibrated predicate confidence and information actions in simulation, while the IROS call supplies relevant interest evidence but no shift validation.
reasoning_summary: The candidate stress-tests the threshold component under calibration shift and uses a joint risk-cost endpoint to prevent trivial always-sense solutions.
cheap_falsifier: Apply lighting and texture shifts to 500 simulator scenes and compare fixed versus temperature-recalibrated thresholds; kill if joint cost does not fall.
main_risk: Post-hoc calibration may require labels unavailable during deployment.

title: Dependency-aware predicate uncertainty for information-gathering plans
current_belief: Spatial predicates in manipulation are correlated, so treating their confidence values independently can misstate plan risk.
proposed_challenge: A dependency model may tighten uncertainty estimates without changing any action decision, adding complexity without operational value.
scientific_question: Does modeling predicate dependencies change information-gathering decisions enough to improve tabletop manipulation success?
falsifiable_claim: A dependency-aware planner will alter at least 10% of sensing decisions and improve task success by at least 5 percentage points over an independence model at matched planning time within 20%; failure of either condition falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied neuro-symbolic study reports tighter dependency-aware bounds and a link between calibration and planning guarantees; the AAAI call supplies broad AI interest evidence only.
reasoning_summary: The candidate requires a behavioral consequence from tighter bounds, directly addressing the possibility that statistical improvement is operationally inert.
cheap_falsifier: Replay 1,000 logged predicate distributions through independent and dependency-aware planners; stop if fewer than 5% of decisions differ.
main_risk: Observed gains may depend on an incorrectly specified predicate graph.

title: Viewpoint-invariant temporal action detection for cross-embodiment demonstrations
current_belief: Action detectors benefit from viewpoint invariance and temporal consistency, but demonstration pipelines often evaluate frame labels rather than downstream robot learning.
proposed_challenge: Invariance may erase embodiment-specific cues needed to infer contact phase or action intent.
scientific_question: Does viewpoint-invariant temporal action detection improve cross-camera robot demonstration segmentation without reducing contact-phase accuracy?
falsifiable_claim: Across two camera viewpoints and two robot embodiments, invariant training will improve segmental F1 by at least 5 points while keeping contact-phase F1 within 2 points of a viewpoint-specific model; failure of either condition falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied action-detection record names viewpoint invariance and temporal consistency as a current method direction, and the CVPR call supplies venue-interest evidence without downstream robot evidence.
reasoning_summary: The candidate makes the transfer target and the potential invariance cost explicit, turning a broad method direction into a two-condition falsification test.
cheap_falsifier: Train on one camera from a small public demonstration set and test a held-out camera; kill if segmental F1 gain is below 2 points or contact boundaries worsen sharply.
main_risk: The supplied literature record lacks an abstract, so the closest-prior overlap remains uncertain and requires audit.

title: Uncertainty-aware weak supervision for robot demonstration boundaries
current_belief: Weakly supervised temporal action localization can use uncertainty and selected knowledge to find action segments without dense labels.
proposed_challenge: Robot demonstrations contain transition and recovery segments that may be systematically discarded as uncertain even though they matter for policy learning.
scientific_question: Does uncertainty-aware segment weighting improve policy learning from weakly labeled robot demonstrations relative to hard segment selection?
falsifiable_claim: Weighting uncertain transition segments will improve downstream task success by at least 5 percentage points over hard selection at matched demonstration count, without reducing action-localization mAP by more than 2 points; failure of either condition falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied weakly supervised localization record provides a direct uncertainty-aware action-segmentation anchor, while the CoRL call establishes robot-learning interest only.
reasoning_summary: The candidate tests whether uncertainty should control loss weight rather than exclusion, using downstream policy success to detect harmful removal of ambiguous but useful transitions.
cheap_falsifier: On one demonstration dataset, compare hard top-confidence segments with continuous uncertainty weights for a small behavior-cloning policy; kill if success is unchanged or worse.
main_risk: Uncertainty may correlate with label noise rather than informative transition structure.

title: Delta-encoded dynamic scene memory for long-horizon robot mapping
current_belief: Per-frame delta encoding can make long dynamic-scene representations compact while maintaining temporally stable rendering.
proposed_challenge: Rendering fidelity may not preserve the geometry and object persistence needed for robot planning after repeated online updates.
scientific_question: Can delta-encoded Gaussian scene memory reduce long-horizon storage without degrading dynamic-obstacle planning relative to full-frame updates?
falsifiable_claim: Over sequences of at least 10,000 frames, delta encoding will reduce scene-memory storage by at least 70% while keeping collision-free planning success within 3 percentage points of full-frame updates; failure of either condition falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied differential 4D Gaussian record reports compact per-frame storage and online updates, while the RSS call supplies robotics interest but no navigation evidence.
reasoning_summary: The candidate changes the outcome from visual fidelity to planning adequacy and makes storage and safety joint acceptance criteria.
cheap_falsifier: Build 1,000-frame memories from one dynamic simulator sequence and replay the same planner; kill if geometry drift raises collisions by more than 5 points.
main_risk: Gaussian reconstruction latency may dominate storage benefits.

title: Frequency-aware temporal fusion for deformable and reflective manipulation perception
current_belief: Uniform temporal smoothing reduces frame discontinuity but can erase high-frequency surface structure needed for reconstruction.
proposed_challenge: Frequency-aware source transport developed for fluid video may not preserve task-relevant geometry under robot camera motion and contact.
scientific_question: Does frequency-aware temporal fusion improve contact-point estimation on reflective or deformable objects relative to uniform temporal smoothing?
falsifiable_claim: Across two object classes, frequency-aware fusion will reduce contact-point error by at least 10% and temporal jitter by at least 15% over uniform smoothing; failure on either class falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied monocular fluid-reconstruction study explicitly balances temporal coherence against high-frequency attenuation, and the CVPR call supplies visual-method interest without manipulation validation.
reasoning_summary: This cross-domain transfer targets the same smoothing-versus-detail conflict but evaluates task geometry rather than appearance.
cheap_falsifier: Apply uniform and three-band temporal fusion to 20 short reflective-object videos with known contact points; stop if error reduction is below 5%.
main_risk: Shallow-water assumptions from the source do not apply to solid or deformable objects.

title: Uncertainty-filtered vibration synthesis for low-data robot contact diagnosis
current_belief: Text-conditioned diffusion with calibrated aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty can filter synthetic vibration samples under domain shift.
proposed_challenge: Uncertainty-filtered augmentation may improve diagnostic classification while failing to preserve control-relevant contact transitions.
scientific_question: Does uncertainty-filtered vibration synthesis improve low-label robot contact-state recognition under sensor and payload shifts?
falsifiable_claim: With at most 20 real examples per contact state, uncertainty-filtered synthetic augmentation will improve shifted-domain macro-F1 by at least 5 points over unfiltered augmentation on both sensor and payload shifts; failure on either shift falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied vibration-diffusion record reports calibrated synthesis and robust downstream augmentation, while the ICRA call provides robot-learning interest but not contact-sensing evidence.
reasoning_summary: The candidate transfers uncertainty-filtered augmentation into robot contact sensing and requires robustness under two physical shifts rather than only fidelity metrics.
cheap_falsifier: Collect or reuse a small vibration set, train with unfiltered versus top-confidence synthetic samples, and kill if shifted macro-F1 gain is below 2 points.
main_risk: Text conditions may not encode the physical variables controlling robot contact spectra.

title: Preparation-aware measurement of micro-offline gains in robot imitation learning
current_belief: Short rest intervals are often credited with offline improvement when performance is measured only during movement execution.
proposed_challenge: Ignoring pre-action planning latency may reverse the sign of apparent learning gains, as demonstrated in the supplied human motor study.
scientific_question: Does including pre-action planning time change the estimated micro-offline learning gain of imitation-trained robot policies?
falsifiable_claim: For at least two sequence-manipulation tasks, including planning latency will reduce the estimated micro-offline gain by at least 50% and reverse its sign in at least one task; failure of both conditions falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied motor-learning record reports a sign reversal when preparation time is included, and the CoRL call supplies interest evidence for robot learning without supporting the transfer.
reasoning_summary: This candidate tests a measurement artifact across biological and robot sequence learning, with the possibility that the direction does not transfer.
cheap_falsifier: Recompute existing robot sequence-learning logs with and without policy-planning latency; kill if gain estimates change by less than 20% in all runs.
main_risk: Robot planning latency may reflect hardware scheduling rather than learned preparation.

title: Adversarial-detection tokens for sensor-shifted embodied vision transformers
current_belief: A dedicated detection token can expose adversarial inputs to a vision transformer without replacing the task representation.
proposed_challenge: Detectors trained on image perturbations may flag benign physical sensor shifts or miss perturbations that cause action changes.
scientific_question: Does a dedicated detection token distinguish action-changing adversarial observations from benign physical shifts in embodied vision transformers?
falsifiable_claim: At 5% false-positive rate on benign lighting, blur, and viewpoint shifts, a detection token will identify at least 70% of observations that change the selected robot action; lower recall falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied detection-token record offers a minimal architectural intervention, and the ECCV call supplies community-interest evidence without embodied robustness results.
reasoning_summary: The candidate evaluates action consequences and benign physical shifts, preventing standard adversarial-image detection accuracy from being mistaken for robot safety evidence.
cheap_falsifier: Attach a detection head to one frozen ViT policy and test 200 adversarial plus 200 benign-shift frames; stop if recall at 5% false positives is below 50%.
main_risk: The supplied literature record lacks an abstract, so exact prior scope and implementation details require verification.

title: Identifiability before mechanistic interpretation of robot policy parameters
current_belief: Named coefficients in an interpretable robot policy are often given mechanistic meaning once the policy predicts actions well.
proposed_challenge: Predictive stability can coexist with poor structural identifiability and weak finite-sample parameter recovery.
scientific_question: Which parameters of an interpretable robot policy remain recoverable from logged observations under correlated task factors?
falsifiable_claim: At least one policy parameter with stable held-out action prediction will have Spearman recovery below 0.3 under correlated factors and will improve above 0.6 after orthogonalizing its designated input; absence of this pattern falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied identifiability study separates semantic interpretation, structural identifiability, practical recovery, and prediction; the AISTATS call supplies methodological interest but not robot-policy evidence.
reasoning_summary: The candidate transfers a reportability hierarchy to interpretable robot policies and requires synthetic ground-truth recovery rather than relying on parameter labels.
cheap_falsifier: Simulate 20 known parameter settings for a small policy under correlated and orthogonalized inputs; kill if all parameters recover above 0.6 in both designs.
main_risk: A synthetic observation model may not represent ambiguity in real robot logs.

title: Single-timebase multimodal state playback for low-power social robots
current_belief: Packing temporally corresponding visual states into one continuously advancing media stream can prevent phase divergence and reduce client workload in conversational avatars.
proposed_challenge: The representation may lose flexibility when robot gaze, gesture, and speech states must respond to unpredictable physical interaction.
scientific_question: Does single-timebase state packing reduce audiovisual-gesture desynchronization on low-power social robots without increasing interaction-response latency?
falsifiable_claim: On a low-power robot, single-timebase packing will reduce 95th-percentile cross-modal phase error by at least 30% while keeping median response latency within 50 ms of independently scheduled streams; failure of either condition falsifies the claim.
why_now: The supplied avatar study reports resource and synchronization advantages together with restricted flexibility, while the IROS call supplies social-robotics interest evidence only.
reasoning_summary: The candidate tests whether a systems representation that removes media-timebase divergence survives the responsiveness requirements of embodied interaction.
cheap_falsifier: Replay scripted speech, gaze, and gesture transitions on an embedded board under both schedulers; kill if phase error improves by less than 15% or latency exceeds the bound.
main_risk: A scripted playback benchmark may understate the flexibility required in live interaction.
